result.title: MASIF: Implicit Failures for Process Observability in Multi-Agent Systems
result.summary: Multi-agent systems (MAS) can complete a task despite local execution errors that are corrected, bypassed, or carried forward without individually determining its outcome. We call these implicit failures (IFs) and study them as signals for process observability beyond final task outcome. Across 1,828 traces from nine MAS-benchmark configurations, IFs occur in 54.3% of successful and 75.2% of failed traces. We develop taxonomies of error types and subsequent absorption mechanisms, supported by human and cross-model annotation audits. Counterfactual replay further probes how repairing an IF changes the final outcome. To examine the practical value of IFs, we evaluate IF-based best-of-N trace selection against existing process reward models, and introduce a novel RL algorithm, IF-GRPO, that uses IF costs to refine preferences among successful trajectories in GRPO. Experiments show that IF-GRPO exhibits some gains in accuracy and process metrics. Importantly, it exposes trade-offs between task performance, IF count and cost, and token-normalized IF density. Overall, our results show that IFs provide complementary process observability into how MAS reach their outcomes, including error recovery, propagation, and IF-based process differences that final task success alone does not expose.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究多智能体系统中的「隐式失败」（局部错误被纠正、绕过或传递而不单独决定任务结果），在1828条轨迹上统计其分布，建立错误类型与吸收机制分类体系，用反事实重放检验修复效果，并提出以失败成本修正成功轨迹偏好的 IF-GRPO。
AI.relevance_reason: 其过程奖励模型、best-of-N 轨迹选择与基于失败成本的偏好修正，可能为 LVR 的轨迹监督、贡献分配与停止/选择决策提供可核查线索，但研究对象是纯文本多智能体流程，与视觉 latent 状态生成无直接联系。
